---
title: "Week 10 Exercises - First Steps on Talapas"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks - about 40 minutes, all on Talapas. Companion reading: [Ch. 20](../book/chapters/20-hpc-talapas.html) and [Ch. 21](../book/chapters/21-parallel-computing.html); reference: [App. I](../book/chapters/appendix-I-slurm.html). You need your Talapas account working (the account check at the end of [Ex 7](Exercises_Week07.qmd)) - if it is not, that is task 0: contact me. **HW2 is due today**; these tasks are the cluster leg of your term project.

1.  Log in to Open OnDemand at <https://ondemand.talapas.uoregon.edu> with your Duck ID and open the **file explorer**. What is the path of your home directory?
2.  Open a **shell** from OnDemand (or `ssh yourduckid@login.talapas.uoregon.edu`) and run `hostname` and `pwd`.
3.  Run `groups` - which PIRG(s) are you in?
4.  Recreate your course skeleton on the cluster: `mkdir -p ~/comptools/{data,scripts,results}`.
5.  Transfer `Stickle_RNAseq.tsv` to `~/comptools/data` (OnDemand's file explorer upload button, or `scp` from your laptop). Confirm with `wc -l`.
6.  Run `module avail R` (press `q` to exit the list), then `module load` an R version and start R on the login node just long enough to run `R.version.string` and quit.
7.  Write a minimal Slurm script `scripts/hello.sbatch` that just prints `hostname` and `date`: start from the batch-script template in the book ([Ch. 20](../book/chapters/20-hpc-talapas.html)), keep the `--job-name`, `--partition`, `--account` and `--time` lines, and drop the rest (including `--output`, so task 8's log gets the default `slurm-*.out` name).
8.  Submit it with `sbatch scripts/hello.sbatch`, watch the queue with `squeue -u $USER`, and when it finishes, `cat` the `slurm-*.out` file. Which node did it run on?
9.  Run `sinfo` and identify one regular partition and the GPU partition.
10. From the shell, run your Week 3 grep pipeline on the dataset - identical commands, bigger computer. That is the point of the shell.
11. Bring your *own* software: `git clone` your project repository onto the cluster (that is why it lives on GitHub), or transfer the `environment.yml` you exported in Week 9. Then `module spider miniconda`, `module load` it, and `conda env create -f environment.yml`.
12. `conda activate rnaseq` and check `which python3` - the same environment as your laptop, built from one text file. Then prove it travels into batch jobs: edit `scripts/hello.sbatch` to `module load` miniconda, `conda activate rnaseq`, and run `python3 -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.__version__)"`, and resubmit. The pandas version in the log is your environment running on a compute node - the full loop, closed.
